newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end lower after devaluation.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end lower after devaluation.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended sharply lower on Tuesday in panic selling after the central bank devalued the rupee 3.79 percent against the dollar.
Dealers said the share index was likely to open lower on Thursday after Wednesday's holiday.

The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index ended 19.87 points, or 1.47 percent, lower at 1,332.14 amid 151 losers and 55 gainers in a turnover of 21.1 million shares, up from Monday's 11.8 million.
"The devaluation led to panic selling by local and foreign institutions on numerous counters," one dealer said.
Pakistan State Oil dropped 12 rupees to 310, Lever Brothers 5.00 to 640, Engro Chemical 5.00 to 135, Shell Pakistan 2.00 to 125, PTCL 0.50 to 33.10 and HUBCO 0.10 to 29.35.
Brooke Bond rose 15.50 to 151 after it announced 290 percent cash dividend for 18 months ended in June. It has already paid 125 percent cash dividend.
